review: The exact excitation matrix is the literal finite Kronecker product of the actual one-copy ground matrix and its complement, selected by B. The copy action is x precomposed with the inverse permutation, and permOp is its actual permutation matrix. Thus reindexing sends B to its direct image. The given stabilizer and original fixed-vector premises are those needed for inheritance; neither commutation nor fixedness of the projected component is assumed. No metric, normalization or spectral certificate is supplied. When the input is unit these established matrices are actual orthogonal excitation projections; the algebraic identities hold more generally, including zero copies.

definitions.definition:
def copyPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) →* Equiv.Perm (Fin k → Ω) where
  toFun σ := Equiv.arrowCongr σ (Equiv.refl Ω)
  map_one' := by ext; rfl
  map_mul' σ τ := by ext; rfl

def permOp (φ : G →* Equiv.Perm X) : G →* Matrix X X ℂ :=
  (Matrix.permMatrixHom (n := X) (R := ℂ)).comp φ

def finKronecker {N : ℕ} {α : Fin N → Type*} [∀ n, Fintype (α n)]
    (A : (n : Fin N) → Matrix (α n) (α n) ℂ) :
    Matrix ((n : Fin N) → α n) ((n : Fin N) → α n) ℂ :=
  Matrix.of fun x y => ∏ n, A n (x n) (y n)
